problems: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Portugal row is ONE state (dynasties are rename events; the 1580-1640 union was personal), not successive states: no split. Its 1581 shape ends where the Iberian Union row (1582-1639) begins, so the dossier has no keyframes for 1582-1639.

Start year set to 1143 (Treaty of Zamora) to follow the county-of-portugal dossier, which ends the county then; the pages count the kingdom from Ourique, 25 July 1139. New keyframe kingdom-of-portugal_1143 (1143-1146) reuses the County of Portugal shape. The integrator may start the kingdom in 1139 instead.

Every shape from 1415 is adjusted to the Cliopatria cells inside modern Portugal: Ceuta, Moroccan stations, Cape Verde, Mina, Sao Tome, Muscat, the Persian Gulf (257 cells 1521-1555 and 1564-1639) and the Angola and Mozambique patches (1824-1910, up to 1.94 M km2) belong to portuguese-empire, portuguese-morocco, portuguese-africa, portuguese-angola and portuguese-mozambique. The 1911 shape (562 km2 at Praia) is wrong.

Madeira (1419) and the Azores (1427) are gains in both this dossier and portuguese-empire: draw once. Cliopatria keeps 15 Muscat cells in this row to 1705 although the Portuguese Empire page has Muscat lost to the Ya'rubids in 1650; the yarubid-dynasty ledger names kingdom-of-portugal as counterpart for 1643 and 1650 and should name portuguese-empire.

WebFetch summaries of the Sancho I, Sancho II and French invasions of Portugal pages were thin; Santarem is dated 15 May 1147 by Afonso I's page footnote but 15 March 1147 in the almoravid-dynasty dossier (from another page).

The Portuguese Empire page says Madeira (1419) and the Azores (1427) were 'reached'; Cliopatria draws Madeira from 1422 and the Azores from 1440/1450 (settlement). The ledger follows the page, the keyframes follow the shape.
